scene.note: One class describes what a boat, a ticket or a crossing is, and each one is an object with values of its own.

steps.note: Bridie wants the seats free on each boat, not one number for the whole river.
The class says what every boat has. Each boat is made with new and keeps its own values.
Asked for its seats free, each boat works it out from its own seats and its own people on board.
A family buys tickets, and Bridie copies the first one for the next person.
The copy is a new ticket with the next person's name and the same fare.

value.label: tickets
values: the first ticket, as it was

steps.note: Two tickets, not two names for one ticket: the first passenger keeps theirs.
Each crossing has an hour and, once Ossian picks one, a boat.
When it has a boat, the crossing gives that boat's name, as the boat is now.
An early crossing has no boat yet. It says so in words instead of falling over.
